### 2026-11-06: # Research

**4.75h**

# Research
## Steppers
I was looking around (researching?) for what to use for the actual power generation bit. I looked at DC motors for a bit but in the end opted to go for steppers. Then i spent a while looking at different places/ websites. I was undecided between the nema 17 and nema 23 so i was just kinda looking at both. I looked in quite a lot of places, like AliExpress, StepperOnline, Ebay and JLCMC (i didn't know there were so many...) .

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/1fc72ce6676e3292eecbe9f1ec45d09be036720fba424a86784a5d0652834fda.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/84134bae60d636a5a33710379e407a7c7ec8782aedc711f6354497240a38bfc5.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/2704e70a45719fd125dc5f782682f05a6b14224c6e65423ec11750e8efcf4a52.png)

In the end i think the ebay one is best. (it is also in GBP btw) this is because of the immense amount of shipping costs. I did decide to go with a nema 23 instead of 17 but it is 2 as heavy. I probably spent to long looking at steppers but i think it was better I got a good one that saved time.

#  Batteries
To be honest when i was looking at batteries i was thinking the cheapest one are best but they are not. i when with some reasonably priced 3000mah 20A 18650 which are good and have decent capacity and high ish discharge rate which will be good for multiple charging outputs.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/f60a8afcce539ce4f8c9c4517a84e85120f426eaf54ee394d06c7fbd33617b4a.png)

# Planning
I also looked at what I will use/ incorporate into the project. i decided I will use a esp32 and screen to act as a stats display. I am planning to make the thing have multiple charging outputs hopefully, probably some usb a and usb c. I might add sth like below to charge devices like phones and earbuds via cable

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/6f7c749fe1373c3869c82d57930326db6a1dd507247f14295d18a3756d06b49c.png)

### 2026-11-07: # PCB schematic

**3h**

# PCB schematic
I started my pcb schematic and found the parts. I spent a while researching to make sure everything would work together. For example, I was originally going to us a 50v max capacitor but i found out the nema 23 could produce up to 60v! Because of this i am also going to add a fuse. I was also looking how best to attach wires from the stepper to my pcb and I figured using screw terminals is a less permanent way but still as secure as directly soldering them on.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/b9bf29545af27a28096f7c2aba3f318dcd91223bc8736354750c60b2dabd7138.png)

# Parts
I also found some of the parts I will need. As i found the parts, mostly on AliExpress, I added them into the schematic. I found bit like 2 pin screw terminal which I'll use and a good fuse to make sure I don't short circuit anything, hopefully...

### 2026-11-08: # PCB done

# PCB done
I wired everything on the PCB up and did the layout. I picked all the parts out and use net ports to connect them together.  I put parts in their own boxes with titles so you can tell what they are. I did the PCB layout so that the components are neatly laid out. I made sure to double check the screw terminals are facing outwards and on the outside of the board so you can access them. I also labelled which bit of the screw terminals is which wire so I know when I am assembling and putting the wires in.

### 2026-11-08: # CAD

**4.75h**

# CAD
## Stepper
I started by deriving the nema 23 stepper into fusion. I got it from grabcad but I had to fix the mistakes. I changed it so the output was a 6.35mm d shaft, originally it was circular which is wrong.

![1000009834](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/16ffc4b9d41374bb0be68b621ce85da87b90cdb7a35c1d9197f69ed38f1fbfa7.png)

## Gears
Then I created the gears with GF Gear Generator, a addon/ utility I installed in fusion. So I created the two gears, a 12T one and a 54T one (T = tooth), that was fairly straightforward, I just need to make sure the module was 1.5, good for printing and a decent thickness, I chose 12mm. Also later, but I'll say now on this topic, but I chamfered the top and bottom of the gear to stop elephant foot, a problem when the edges of the gears splay outward.

![1000009835](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/534059aa1eafb96d686e04f61804985f04c0ce7a00c3d7fb5aef750eb2f3d678.png)
## Mounting
When I was figuring how to mount the gears, I decided to use a faceplate attached to the stepper with a hole for the bearing to slot into. The are alignment rods of one side to fix the plate to the stepper. The plate also wraps around the doors of the stepper.

![1000009837](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/38aa1e29eef8c1574b3a5dc3d38c1b214cd1118ccfb131926a662e40cc6a0a70.png)
## Handle
The handle is made up of two parts. The main bit which attaches to the large gear via alignment pins and M3 screws and the knob which is attached via a bearing at the end of the handle. The entire handle is about 90mm long to give a balance of leverage and turning comfort. I made the knob bit to have a pin/ bit sticking out the bottom to fit into a bearing so it can spin easier. There is also a cut out with tolerances in the main handle for the bearing to push fit inside.

![1000009836](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/5a815bacfc27a1923f11057685fe58209336d1b077b82f667824bcd35d8056de.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/cbe92b15b1c94b8379b1a03e6862fdf99c1efc60869272706020f432f3db5b9a.png)

### 2026-11-09: # Changing the PCB

**5h**

# Changing the PCB
I was going to do a case and finish the CAD. But I couldn't think of a good small layout for the entire thing, mainly because the PCB was 75x75mm and the the capacitor protruded off it another 40mm so took up a lot of bulk. And the buck converter has heat sinks and stuff so that is quite bulky too. So in the end I redesigned the PCB to make it 60x65 which is nearly the same width as the nema 23 so it should fit next to it snugly. I did not change the schematic and only changed the layout. I had to double check the size of the capacitor because the one in my PCB 3d view was just a placeholder and not the actual thing so it was massively oversized for some reason. If you look at the face plate of the nema 23 it is about that size + 5mm on one side so quite small. The capacitor is not as big as  in the 3D view btw...

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/91HF73JHUwEio9xtrq7tRJvOd8KiT0lT/c90d8344b91f4a2db18682531d47b61da46dcb38abaa27bc92d0951b353bd816.png)
